Subject: FinWorks post-call: fit evaluation, model deltas, and snapshot safety ladder

Hi Elena / Greg — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single plan: 

Summary of needs we heard
- Primary: reliable decisioning for loan approval flows (high precision on denial reasons).
- Secondary: consistent tone and brief explanations for audit logs.
- Risk: small sample of edge prompts produced materially different outputs after a recent model rollout.

What we recommend for the POC / eval window
- Candidate models: redwood-3b-v1 (baseline), redwood-3b-q4f (latency/cost-optimized quantized variant), redwood-7b-instruct (higher-capacity option for complex cases).
- Eval artifacts attached: finworks-eval-pack.zip (benchmark prompts + scoring harness), prompt-sets.md (production prompt templates), benchmark-summary.pdf (token-level latency + quality summary).
- Safety ladder: propose taking a snapshot of the current production snapshot (model: redwood-3b-v1@20280306) and pinning it for FinWorks during the trial if you want absolute consistency. Pining + a canary plan gives you both stability and a path to test newer releases.

Immediate ask
- Can you confirm whether you want us to pin the current snapshot for your sandbox/test org? If yes, we can schedule the pin within 24 hours and provide a diff report for any subsequent releases.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Your confirmation on pin vs. allow auto-updates (reply to this thread)
2) We run a snapshot + generate a short diff report (we'll circulate within 24 hours)
3) If you approve, we pin the snapshot for the POC and run a 48-hour canary with the quantized variant to validate latency/cost tradeoffs

I've attached the eval pack and prompt sets. Sharing the HubSpot deal and a Drive link below for internal docs.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow if you'd prefer a screen-share.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

https://redwood.com/

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear follow-up. Two quick notes from our side: 

1) We did see a concrete regression in one of our sampled decision prompts after what we assume was a routine model update on Mar 6. Example (anonymized):

--- example prompt ---
Customer: "I have a 720 FICO and make $110k/yr, do I qualify for the standard small-business loan?"
Previous model response: "Prelim approval likely; request income docs and verify address."
New model response: "Refer to underwriting manual; may require additional docs."
--- end ---

The newer response added friction and changed the likelihood estimate in a way that affected our automated routing to human review. We need to understand the delta and would prefer a snapshot if possible while we complete deeper testing.

2) When you say "pin" — are there costs or lead times we should expect? We want this pinned for the remainder of the 30-day POC if feasible.

We can confirm by EOD whether we prefer pinning; if it helps, please prepare the diff report and an outline of options (pin vs staged rollback vs canary).

- Elena Park
Head of Product, FinWorks
epark@finworks.com | +1 (212) 555-0220

Hi all — quick status and proposed remedial plan. Attached: diff-report.csv (top 25 prompt diffs).

Key findings (top-line)
- The change that likely produced the regression is localized to the decoding temperature/penalty defaults applied to system prompts between snapshots 20280301 and 20280306; architecture and weights unchanged.
- Of 250 sampled production prompts from FinWorks, 18 showed materially different routing recommendations (probability shift that would flip automated routing).

Immediate options (tradeoffs listed)
A) Pin snapshot redwood-3b-v1@20280306 for FinWorks (recommended for POC stability)
   - Lead time: we can apply a customer-scoped pin within 24 hours and lock auto-updates for your org.
   - Cost: typical pin surcharge applies (one-time snapshot capture + minor monthly pin fee) — Laura will add the precise numbers in a follow-up.
   - Rollback: to remove the pin we simply unpin and optionally apply a staged canary; no code changes on your side.

B) Staged rollback to prior defaults (if you prefer not to pin)
   - We can replicate the prior decoding defaults in a new compatible snapshot and route your traffic to it; this requires a brief canary (6–12 hours) and additional validation.

C) Canary + quantized variant test
   - Run redwood-3b-q4f in canary to confirm latency/cost improvements and check whether quantization masks the behavior change.

Proposed action (my recommended path)
1) If you want absolute parity for the POC: confirm "PIN" in reply and we'll apply redwood-3b-v1@20280306 as a customer-scoped pin within 24 hours.
2) Simultaneously we run a 48-hour canary with redwood-3b-q4f to see cost/latency delta and capture any additional diffs.
3) Deliver a short post-canary report with the recommended long-term path (pin+gradual upgrade vs keep pinned until GA).

I've attached the diff-report.csv to this message and linked the detailed internal diff report here: https://redwood-internal/reports/diffs/FW-2028-003-20280309

If you confirm PIN, Vanessa I can trigger the scoped pin and schedule the canary. Elena/Greg — happy to take a 20-min screen-share to walk through the diffs if helpful.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
